source_title: Speedy Hire Plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 115 and 149 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors on 24 May 2021; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: COVID-19 reduced revenue excluding disposals 10.7%, EBITA 35.0%, adjusted profit before tax 40.7% and EBITA margin from 9.6% to 7.0%. The Group permanently closed 13 depots, consolidated 22 into larger locations and made about 200 roles redundant. Trading recovered strongly, operating cash rose 13%, net debt fell from £79.3m to £33.2m and leverage halved to 0.5x.
already_announced_exclusion: The 13 depot closures, 22-depot consolidation programme, approximately 200 redundancies and Middle East asset sale and exit disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Revenue, profit and margin contraction indicate high operating pressure, partly offset by strong second-half recovery, improved operating cash, material deleveraging and substantial facility headroom.

source_title: Speedy Hire Plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 144 and 178 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors on 30 June 2023; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 13.9% and adjusted profit before tax 6.6%, but gross and EBITDA margins fell, a £20.4m non-itemised-asset write-off and £6.7m restructuring charge reduced statutory profit before tax to £1.8m. Net debt rose to £92.4m and leverage to 1.3x, while free cash flow recovered, facility headroom remained £83.5m and underlying end markets were positive.
already_announced_exclusion: The non-itemised-asset write-off and remedial controls, net 20-depot rationalisation, related redundancies and logistics restructuring disclosed or implemented before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The control failure, exceptional charges, statutory-profit collapse, margin dilution and higher debt create substantial pressure, offset by underlying revenue and adjusted-profit growth, positive cash flow and ample liquidity.
